drawer.title: GEO readiness
drawer.subtitle: Can AI crawlers actually read this page?

verdict.ok: Every crawler we tested can read this page.
verdict.thin: Some crawlers receive far less text than a browser. The page may need JavaScript to show its content.
verdict.unpublished: This page has never been published, so there is no public URL to test yet.
verdict.empty: Even a browser receives almost no text before JavaScript runs ({{count}} words). Crawlers will see an empty page.

crawler.initialHtml: What the crawler receives before JavaScript runs

explain.403: The server refused this crawler. This is usually a firewall or bot-protection rule, not a content problem.
explain.jsOnly: A browser sees much more text than the crawler does. The content probably arrives through JavaScript, which crawlers do not run.
explain.empty: The initial HTML is a shell. The content arrives through JavaScript, or after a client-side redirect, and crawlers do not run either. Server-side rendering is the fix, not a robots.txt change.
explain.blockedButAllowed: Your robots.txt allows {{count}} of these crawlers, but the server refused them anyway. The block is coming from a firewall or bot protection, not from your content or your robots.txt. This is an infrastructure fix.
explain.reachableButDisallowed: Your robots.txt tells {{count}} of these crawlers not to fetch this page. They can reach it, but a well-behaved crawler will not read it. Change robots.txt if you want them to.

crawler.metaRefresh: Client-side redirect: the page tells a browser to go to {{url}}. Crawlers stay on this shell.

error.generic: The check could not be completed.
error.rateLimit: Too many checks in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
error.notPublished: Publish this page first, then run the check.

robots.title: robots.txt
robots.absent: This site has no robots.txt. Every crawler is allowed everywhere by default. That works, but nobody decided it.
robots.noneNamed: No AI crawler is named in robots.txt. They all fall under the wildcard rule, so they are allowed by default rather than on purpose.
robots.someNamed: {{count}} AI crawler is named explicitly in robots.txt.
robots.someNamed_plural: {{count}} AI crawlers are named explicitly in robots.txt.
robots.someDisallowed: {{count}} of them cannot fetch this page.

control.title: Control AI crawlers
control.intro: Sets each crawler's site-wide stance in robots.txt. Groups you have not changed are left exactly as they are, comments and Sitemap lines included.
control.applied: Written and published. Run the check again to see it.
control.cannotWrite: You do not have permission to change this site's settings.
control.noMixin: This site has no robots.txt yet. Applying will create one.
control.placeholder: What is stored is the module's placeholder, not a real file.
control.error: robots.txt could not be read or written.
control.rule: Blocking replaces that crawler's rules with a site-wide refusal. Allowing only undoes a site-wide refusal: a crawler with path rules such as Disallow: /docs/ is left alone, because flattening that would throw away work. A crawler sharing a group with others is moved into its own group so the others keep their rules.
control.accessExplain: robots.txt states a policy. Only a fetch shows whether the server honours it.
control.verdictServed: All {{count}} AI crawlers are served by this site
control.verdictRefused: {{count}} AI crawler is refused by the server
control.verdictRefused_plural: {{count}} AI crawlers are refused by the server
control.verdictAgree: robots.txt and the server agree on every crawler.
control.verdictMismatch: {{count}} crawler is treated differently from what robots.txt says. One of the two is wrong.
control.verdictMismatch_plural: {{count}} crawlers are treated differently from what robots.txt says. One of the two is wrong.

bot.GPTBot: Collects pages to train OpenAI's models. Blocking it does not affect whether ChatGPT can cite you.
bot.OAI-SearchBot: Builds the index behind ChatGPT's search results. Blocking it takes you out of those answers.
bot.ChatGPT-User: Fetches a page when someone asks ChatGPT about it. Blocking it means ChatGPT cannot open your pages on request.
bot.ClaudeBot: Collects pages to train Anthropic's models. Blocking it does not affect whether Claude can cite you.
bot.Claude-SearchBot: Builds the index behind Claude's search. Blocking it takes you out of those answers.
bot.PerplexityBot: Builds Perplexity's search index. Blocking it takes you out of its answers.
bot.Perplexity-User: Fetches a page when someone asks Perplexity about it.
bot.Google-Extended: Controls whether your content trains Gemini and grounds its answers. It does not affect Google Search ranking.
bot.GoogleOther: A general-purpose Google crawler used by several product teams. Its exact use is not published.
bot.Bingbot: Builds the Bing index, which also grounds Microsoft Copilot. Blocking it takes you out of both.
bot.CCBot: Collects pages for Common Crawl, a public dataset many models train on.
bot.Bytespider: Collects pages to train ByteDance's models.
bot.Amazonbot: Crawls for Alexa answers and Amazon search.
bot.Applebot-Extended: Controls whether your content trains Apple Intelligence. It does not affect Siri or Spotlight results.
bot.meta-externalagent: Collects pages to train Meta's models.

control.searchBlockedTitle: {{count}} crawler that answers questions is blocked
control.searchBlockedTitle_plural: {{count}} crawlers that answer questions are blocked
control.searchBlocked: Blocking a crawler that builds answers removes you from that assistant's replies. Blocking one that only trains models does not. Check this is what you meant: {{names}}.

llms.title: llms.txt
llms.absent: No llms.txt at the site root (HTTP {{status}}). AI engines have no curated map of your best content.
llms.servedHtml: The site returned an HTML page for /llms.txt instead of a text file. That counts as not having one.

generate.title: Generate from the page tree
generate.intro: Builds the file from published pages, their titles and their descriptions. No model, no external service: the same site always produces the same file.
generate.unchanged: Identical to what is already stored. Nothing to apply.
generate.differs: This differs from what is stored. Review it before applying.
generate.placeholder: What is stored is the module's placeholder, not a real file.
generate.noMixin: The site has no llms.txt yet. Applying will create one.
generate.cannotWrite: You do not have permission to change this site's settings.
generate.applied: Written and published. Run the check again to see it.
generate.rule: Pages hidden from the navigation are left out, and descriptions are never invented. Edit the text before applying if you want something different: what you see is exactly what gets written.

files.editedInSettings: robots.txt and llms.txt belong to the whole site. Edit them under Additional, SEO, GEO readiness.

score.headline: {{passed}} of {{total}} checks passed
score.allGood: Everything we can check from here passes.
score.rubric: Each check reads one fact already in this report. Being disallowed in robots.txt is not counted as a failure: refusing a crawler is a legitimate choice. A disagreement between the policy and the server is.

reachable.label: Every AI crawler gets the page
reachable.fix: At least one crawler was refused. That is usually a firewall or bot-protection rule rather than a content problem.

policyMatchesReality.label: robots.txt matches what the server does
policyMatchesReality.fix: The policy and the server disagree for at least one crawler. One of the two is wrong, and the report names which.

noClientRedirect.label: No client-side redirect
noClientRedirect.fix: The page tells a browser to go elsewhere. Crawlers do not follow that, so this shell is all they read.

namedInRobots.label: AI crawlers named in robots.txt
namedInRobots.fix: No AI crawler is named. They fall to the wildcard group, so you have no explicit policy for them.

contentInInitialHtml.label: Real text in the initial HTML
contentInInitialHtml.fix: The page returns almost no text before JavaScript runs. Server-side rendering is the fix, not a robots.txt change.

sameContentForCrawlers.label: Crawlers get the same text as a browser
sameContentForCrawlers.fix: At least one crawler receives far less text than the browser did. Check what the server varies on the user agent.

title.label: Title present and a usable length
title.fix: A title under 10 or over 70 characters is either uninformative or truncated wherever it is quoted.

singleH1.label: Exactly one H1
singleH1.fix: Zero or several H1 headings leave the main subject of the page ambiguous.

headingOutline.label: Sub-headings structure the page
headingOutline.fix: Retrieval splits pages on headings. A page with no H2 is one undifferentiated block.

metaDescription.label: Meta description present
metaDescription.fix: Without it the summary shown alongside an answer is generated from whatever text comes first.

canonical.label: Canonical URL declared
canonical.fix: Without a canonical, the same content reachable at several addresses is treated as several pages.

langDeclared.label: Page language declared
langDeclared.fix: The html lang attribute is missing, so the language has to be guessed. On a multilingual site that is a real risk.

structuredData.label: Structured data present
structuredData.fix: No JSON-LD was found. Schema types are the most direct way to state what this page is about.

freshness.label: Modification date published
freshness.fix: No dateModified was found. Assistants weigh recency, and an undated page cannot show it is current.

imageAlt.label: Images carry alt text
imageAlt.fix: Some images have no alt text. To a text-only crawler those images simply do not exist.

robotsPresent.label: robots.txt is served
robotsPresent.fix: No robots.txt. Everything is allowed by default, which is a decision you did not get to make.

llmsPresent.label: llms.txt is served
llmsPresent.fix: No llms.txt. It is the one file that tells an assistant which pages matter and why.

guestReadable.label: A visitor with no account can read it
guestReadable.fix: A guest cannot read this page, so no crawler ever will. Some servers answer a gated page with a login form and a 200, which looks like success. Check the page's access restrictions.

score.fromTemplate: Comes from the template “{{template}}”, which renders {{count}} pages. Fixing it there fixes all of them.

diff.identical: No change. The file would be written exactly as it is now.

dashboard.title: GEO readiness for site {{site}} - {{language}}
dashboard.intro: The two files that tell AI crawlers what to do with this site: robots.txt states the policy, llms.txt says which pages matter and why. Both belong to the whole site, so they are edited here rather than from a page.

visibility.title: Content no AI can read
visibility.intro: Published pages that a visitor with no account cannot read. A crawler served a login form gets a cheerful 200 and reports success, so only the repository knows these pages are invisible.
visibility.summary: {{readable}} of {{scanned}} published pages can be read by a visitor with no account
visibility.noFindings: Every published page can be read without an account.
visibility.truncated: Only the first {{scanned}} pages were scanned. The rest were not looked at.
visibility.deliberateIntro: Pages inside a branch that is closed as a whole, which normally means a members area rather than a mistake.
visibility.error: The scan could not be completed.

kind.hiddenByCondition: Hidden right now by a visibility condition
kind.noindex: Set to noindex, so it will not be cited

visibility.noindexTitle: This page is set to noindex
visibility.noindex: Search engines and AI crawlers are told not to index this page, so it will not be cited. That is often deliberate for legal or utility pages. If it is not, the setting is on the page itself.
visibility.gatedTitle: No visitor can read this page
visibility.gated: A visitor with no account cannot open this page, so no AI crawler ever will. Some servers answer a gated page with a login form and a 200, which looks like success from outside. The setting is in the page's access restrictions.

score17.title: Site score
score17.intro: Every published page scored, one fetch each, on a schedule you set. The per-page drawer fetches as sixteen crawlers to compare them; doing that site-wide would be hundreds of thousands of requests, so a scan fetches once per page as a single AI crawler.
score17.headline: {{percent}}% of checks pass across the site
score17.up: up {{n}} points since the last run
score17.down: down {{n}} points since the last run
score17.counts: {{scored}} pages scored · {{critical}} with a critical failure · {{unreadable}} no visitor can read
score17.failed: The run did not finish. The server log has the detail.
score17.scheduleHelp: A Quartz cron expression, in the server's timezone. Leave the scope empty to scan the whole site, or give a path to scan one branch. A running scan appears in the administration job list.
score17.badCron: That is not a cron expression Quartz accepts. Nothing was saved.
score17.rateLimit: Too many scans in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
score17.error: The scan state could not be read.
score17.truncated: The scan stopped at {{pages}} pages. Narrow the scope, or raise the limit.
score17.enabledHelp: When off, the site is only scanned when you press Scan now.
score17.cronHelp: Runs in the server's timezone, not your browser's.
score17.scopeHelp: Leave empty for the whole site, or choose a branch to scan only that part.
score17.whyFewer: 17 checks here, 18 in the page drawer. Comparing what a crawler receives against what a browser receives needs a second fetch of the same page, so “{{check}}” is only evaluated one page at a time. Both counts report the same failures.
score17.byTemplateHelp: A check is blamed on the template only when it fails on nearly every page that template renders. Three pages failing out of four hundred is three authors; four hundred out of four hundred is the template.
score17.templateClean: Nothing here is the template's fault.

sitemap.title: Sitemap against reality
sitemap.agrees: All {{entries}} entries resolve to published content, and nothing published is missing from it.
sitemap.notListedTitle: This page is not in the sitemap
sitemap.notListed: The site publishes a sitemap and this page is not in it, so a crawler has no reason to look for it.

kind.missing: Published, but not in the sitemap
kind.unknown: In the sitemap, but nothing published answers
kind.staleDate: The date in the sitemap is wrong
kind.noindexListed: Listed in the sitemap and marked noindex

why.missing: A crawler has no reason to look for these.
why.unknown: Crawl budget spent on addresses that lead nowhere.
why.staleDate: Claiming a page is older than it is tells crawlers not to bother recrawling it. Shown as claimed then actual.
why.noindexListed: The map says index this, the page says do not. One of the two is a mistake.

sitemap.counts: {{entries}} entries in the sitemap · {{published}} published pages and content items a visitor can read.
sitemap.noindexListedTitle: This page is in the sitemap and marked noindex
sitemap.noindexListedPage: The sitemap tells crawlers to index this page and the page itself tells them not to. One of the two is a mistake.
sitemap.staleTitle: The sitemap's date for this page is wrong
sitemap.stalePage: The sitemap claims {{detail}}. A crawler that trusts the earlier date has no reason to come back for what changed.
sitemap.intro: What the sitemap says against what the site actually publishes. Entries are resolved against the repository rather than fetched, so this costs no requests and needs no site scan. The scheduled scan refreshes it too.
sitemap.never: Run a check, or wait for the next scheduled site scan, which refreshes this too.
sitemap.limits: Entries are matched to content, not fetched, so a redirect is not detected: an entry that redirects elsewhere counts as resolving. Every language of the site is compared, and each finding names the URL it belongs to.

error.failed: The sitemap could not be read or compared. The server log has the detail.
error.rate: Wait a moment before checking again.

absent.none: Nothing answers {{url}} (HTTP {{status}}), so crawlers are handed no map of this site at all. The Sitemap module publishes one per site.
absent.notSitemapTitle: That address answers, but not with a sitemap
absent.notSitemap: {{url}} returns HTTP {{status}}, but the response is not a sitemap - most often a page or an error page served with a success code. Until that address returns a real sitemap, crawlers have no usable map, and nothing here can be compared.
absent.unreachableTitle: The sitemap could not be reached
absent.unreachable: {{url}} could not be fetched at all, so whether a sitemap exists is unknown. This is a connection problem, not a finding about your content.

links.title: Pages nothing links to
links.intro: A crawler can tell you what it found. It cannot tell you what it missed, because it never knew the page existed. This compares everything published against everything the site actually links to, using the rendered HTML of each page the last scan fetched.
links.counts: {{pages}} published pages judged, from {{read}} pages read in this language.
links.never: The link graph is built from the rendered HTML of every page, so it comes from a site scan. Run one from the Site score tab.
links.allLinkedTitle: Every page is linked from somewhere
links.allLinked: No published page in this language is unreachable, and none depends on the menus alone.

kind.orphans: Nothing links here, and the sitemap does not list it
kind.weak: Reachable, but nobody chose to link it

why.orphans: No page links to these and no sitemap entry names them. Nothing will ever find them.
why.weak: A crawler can reach these, but only through a menu that lists everything or through the sitemap. No author linked to them, and link-weighted crawlers treat that as a weak signal.

links.limits: Links are read from rendered HTML, so a menu built from the page tree, a listing, a rich text link and a configured button all count the same. One link per source page: linking twice from the same page is one decision. Only the language of this scan is judged, since only its pages were fetched. Your home page is never reported.
links.orphanPage: No other published page links here and the sitemap does not list it, so a crawler has no way to discover it at all.
links.navOnlyTitle: Only the menu links to this page
links.navOnlyPage: It appears in navigation on {{count}} pages, but no page links to it from its content. Crawlers that weight links treat a menu entry as a weaker signal than a link an author chose to make.
